A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAT-STEER and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. Matching moved and renumbered content supports a reliable comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA and HelpSteer experiments, generalization evaluations, component ablations, and token-selection analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds ParaDetox diagnostics, further component ablations, and HH-RLHF and OpenBookQA evaluations.

M1.justification: The gating function, MMD alignment, positive-preservation and sparsity penalties, orthogonality penalty, and activation normalization are retained. The explanation of soft orthogonality clarifies the existing objective rather than changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds toxic/neutral text evaluation on ParaDetox, transfer to helpful-and-harmless assistant queries on HH-RLHF, and structured reasoning through OpenBookQA. These substantially broaden the evaluated inputs and task requirements beyond the retained trustworthiness QA, HelpSteer generation, and FaithEval coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched benchmark experiments. The new HH-RLHF and OpenBookQA comparisons reuse ICL, SFT, and LITO; they introduce no new baseline method. Additional component-removal variants extend the ablation analysis.

E3.justification: New protocols include diagnostics on 100 toxic and 100 neutral ParaDetox samples, HH-RLHF evaluation using QA-trained steering vectors, and OpenBookQA evaluation measuring accuracy loss on the original tasks. Separately, Sections 4.1-4.2 and Figure 3 change the reported HelpSteer judge from GPT-4 to GPT-4o while retaining identical scores; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that evaluation was rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds direct measurements of attribute-specific gating, intervention counts, and toxicity reduction. The existing ablation moves from Appendix B, Table 2, to Section 5, Table 3, and gains separate removals of positive preservation, sparsity, and orthogonality from the full method. Appendix C also adds an OpenBookQA study of performance retention on previously evaluated tasks.

E5.justification: No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting is introduced. Matched plots retain their presentation, and the added tables report point values. ParaDetox sample selection does not establish repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values are retained, while v2 adds an 86% ParaDetox toxicity reduction, three component-removal scores, HH-RLHF win rates of 67.07%, 62.35%, and 59.12% against ICL, SFT, and LITO, and 77.46% OpenBookQA accuracy with a 0.32-point average decline on original tasks. The new ablation prose incorrectly attributes a 3.86-point drop to positive-preservation removal: Table 3 implies 4.57 points; 3.86 corresponds to sparsity removal.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(10), the formal objectives, and the MMD kernel formulation are retained. The soft-orthogonality discussion explains the existing penalty without introducing or revising a formal constraint, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about selective multi-attribute steering, comparative performance, data efficiency, and generalization. The added experiments provide supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains that soft orthogonality permits beneficial overlap between semantically related attributes. A new Limitations section acknowledges complex or unsteerable attributes, dependence on steering data, restricted evaluation scope, and residual risks. Appendix C additionally interprets the OpenBookQA accuracy-versus-retention tradeoff.

D1.justification: V2 specifies d=4096 and documents reuse of QA-trained steering vectors for the new analyses and continued SFT training from the three-task checkpoint for OpenBookQA. Appendix A's preprocessing, layer choices, hyperparameters, and hardware remain unchanged, as does the code-access disclosure.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Bai et al. (2022), Logacheva et al. (2022), Mihaylov et al. (2018), and Jiang et al. (2024) for the new datasets and reasoning context. Section 6 and the central positioning relative to prompting, fine-tuning, and intervention methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision adds localized explanatory passages and a Limitations section, moves the ablation discussion into Section 5, expands Appendix C, and corrects its heading. Most existing prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds three compact tables, expands and relocates the ablation table, and reflows existing tables and figures. All seven figure graphics retain their designs and plotted content; Figure 3's caption updates the judge name. The two-column visual format remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's existing ablations and transfer tests, v2 provides more direct evidence about gating behavior, individual penalties, and performance retention when adding reasoning tasks. Its soft-orthogonality explanation and limitations also better qualify applicability. These improve support for the existing claims, although uncertainty reporting is not strengthened and the new ablation explanation misattributes the 3.86-point decline. The net quality gain is useful but limited.
